_comment: EXAMPLE — one agent call. Stage 3 writes <output>/threats/<use case id>/<LETTER>.json, one per STRIDE letter, and skips any that already exists unless --force. That per-letter granularity is the cache unit: re-running Repudiation alone costs one call, not six. Stage 4 reads the merged ../UC-LOGIN.json instead of these.

threats.title: Credential stuffing against an unthrottled login endpoint
threats.description: The login route compares credentials with no rate limit, lockout, or CAPTCHA, so an attacker may guess passwords without bound.
threats.attack_scenario: The attacker replays a breach corpus of email/password pairs against POST /rest/user/login. With no throttling, a few thousand requests surface accounts whose owners reused a password.

evidence.snippet: const user = await models.User.findOne({ where: { email, password: hash(password) } })

threats.recommendation: Rate limit the login route by both source address and target account, and add escalating delay after repeated failures.

threats.title: Session identifier not rotated on successful authentication
threats.description: No session regeneration was located on the authentication path, leaving any pre-login identifier valid afterwards.
threats.attack_scenario: The attacker plants a known session identifier in the victim's browser, waits for the victim to authenticate, then reuses that identifier to act as them.
threats.recommendation: Regenerate the session identifier immediately after a successful credential check.

_notes.risk: DERIVED, never assigned: likelihood x impact through the fixed matrix in main/contract.py. high x high = critical, medium x high = high. A threat whose risk disagrees with its inputs is rejected and the call retried.
_notes.confidence: 'high' REQUIRES at least one evidence entry with a real file and line. 'low' with an empty evidence array is correct and expected when the code could not be located — see T-UC-LOGIN-S-002. Inventing a plausible path to justify high confidence is the failure this rule exists to prevent.
_notes.id: T-<use case id>-<LETTER>-<nnn>, numbered from 001 within each call.
_notes.dfd_element.type: Must be one the letter actually analyzes. Spoofing accepts external_entity and process only; a Spoofing threat against a data_store is rejected.
_notes.status: unmitigated | partial | mitigated. Keep mitigated threats — they show which controls already exist.
